data.description:
## Context

DSO's per-step HARD-GATE workflows (COMMIT, REVIEW) currently express compliance as prose inside the workflow docs. A bot-psychologist Probe B (sycophancy probe against a fresh sub-agent) confirmed the gate is reachable when an agent is challenged but is not load-bearing during silent autonomous execution: agents batch steps, skip advisory breadcrumb writes, drop classifier-flagged overlay dispatches (bug 94e8-9f91), pipe validation output through truncating filters that mask diagnostics, and never write the breadcrumb log (bug 7b41-3061). A user reporter on a host .NET project experienced this across multiple sessions before catching it manually. The same psychology was hardened on the reviewer surface in closed epic db68-ca95; this epic is its orchestrator-side counterpart.

The single outcome of this epic is: ship a load-bearing pre-commit verifier gate that is safe to deploy in production sessions — meaning (a) the gate enforces the right thing, (b) agents cannot silently bypass it, (c) the gate has a sane override path so legitimate commits aren't permanently blocked when the gate is wrong, (d) the gate has zero false positives on existing valid commit paths.

## Success Criteria

- SC1 — Verifier as load-bearing pre-commit gate. A new pre-commit hook (parity tier with existing test-gate / review-gate) reads the breadcrumb log and wrapper-written validation artifacts for the worktree where the commit is being made and refuses the commit when (a) any expected artifact is missing for a step that should have run under the active enforcement.strategy and SKIP_REVIEW state, or (b) the classifier flagged one or more REVIEW overlays without their corresponding findings artifacts. Test fixtures: synthetically removing a wrapper artifact triggers the block; synthetic missing overlay findings file (with classifier-flagged overlay) triggers the block. Regression tests reproduce the failure surfaces of bugs 94e8-9f91 (overlay flags ignored) and 7b41-3061 (empty breadcrumb log) and confirm both are mechanically prevented as a direct consequence of SC1's enforcement.

- SC2 — Truncation-masking immunity. Validation commands (test, format, lint, classifier dispatch, reviewer dispatch) run through wrappers that capture full output into result artifacts. The verifier reads from the artifact, not from the agent's terminal stream. Test fixture: an agent invoking the wrapper with `2>&1 | tail -3` (or any other agent-side output filter) does not change what the verifier sees and does not allow a hidden lint/test failure to slip through.

- SC3 — Per-commit interactive override path (release-blocking precondition for SC1). A hard-blocking gate is unsafe to deploy without a sane escape hatch for legitimate commits the gate gets wrong. Override is reachable only via explicit `dso commit-override --reason="<text>"` invoked by the user (not the agent). Override applies to exactly one commit attempt and writes a durable audit record (in $ARTIFACTS_DIR and as a comment/trailer on the commit) listing the missing artifacts and the user's reason. Test fixture: a single override clears the next commit; a second attempt without re-authorization is blocked again. Cross-epic constraint: when dso-fbky autonomous mode is active, dso commit-override returns an error and the hook still blocks.

- SC4 — Worktree-context safety in all three execution contexts. Verifier and wrappers behave correctly when commit runs in (a) the main repo, (b) a session worktree, (c) an isolated sub-agent worktree harvested back via the existing harvest-worktree.sh / record-test-status.sh --attest paths. Verifier reads artifacts only from the worktree where the commit is being made; sub-agent artifacts reach it only through the existing harvest path. A wrapper invoked from a CWD that does not match the worktree it would write to fails fast with a clear error rather than silently writing to a sibling worktree's artifacts dir. Test fixtures cover all three contexts plus the misconfigured-CWD failure mode.

- SC5 — Conditional-step skip markers and zero false-positive baseline. Legitimately-skipped steps (e.g., enforcement.strategy=ci, SKIP_REVIEW=true, commands.test_changed unset) emit explicit `skipped:<reason>` artifacts that the verifier accepts. A passing run of validate.sh --ci and a clean DSO-self-commit on this epic demonstrate the verifier introduces zero false positives on existing valid commit paths — the gate fires only on actual non-compliance.

## Dependencies

None blocking.

This epic blocks: af26-dd5a-df6d-4f81 (forbidden-action HARD-GATE follow-on; reuses the override-path infrastructure, artifacts-dir resolution, and audit-trail pattern delivered here) and f61f-7e0a-36d3-4e7d (per-story PR review with incremental attestation; f61f's attestation strategy must build on this epic's verifier — clarified during f61f's own brainstorm).

Subsumed: bugs 94e8-9f91 (overlay flags silently dropped) and 7b41-3061 (breadcrumb log empty) close as a direct consequence of SC1 — no separate work axis.

Related, not blocking: closed epic db68-ca95 (reviewer-side AI-blindspot hardening — same psychology, different surface).

## Approach

Wrapper-driven artifact verification (Option A from Phase 2). Each per-step validation command (test, format, lint, classifier dispatch, reviewer dispatch) is invoked through a thin wrapper (`.claude/scripts/dso commit-step <name>`) that runs the underlying command, captures the full output, and atomically writes a result artifact alongside the breadcrumb. A new pre-commit hook reads the artifacts (not agent stdout) and refuses commits with missing artifacts, missing overlay findings, or visible truncation markers. Override is reachable only via `dso commit-override --reason="..."` invoked by the user. The verifier resolves artifacts via get_artifacts_dir() of the worktree where commit happens; cross-worktree artifact transfer remains via the existing harvest-worktree.sh / --attest mechanism — no new cross-worktree paths.

## Cross-Epic Interactions

- Resource: per-commit override mechanism. Interaction: dso-fbky autonomous mode must NOT bypass this epic's verifier or override path. Gate: when autonomous mode is active, dso commit-override returns an error and the hook still blocks on missing artifacts.
- Resource: artifacts-dir / harvest atomicity. Interaction: 70f6-05f1 parallel-worktree review introduces N concurrent harvests. Gate: harvest into a target worktree's artifacts dir is atomic per-target; verifier does not race when multiple sub-agent worktrees harvest concurrently.
- Resource: reviewer-findings artifact family. Interaction: dbbc-cf67-8cfc-4b4d stateful re-review persists multi-cycle review state. Gate: overlay-dispatch verification reads the latest cycle's classifier output and findings files; multi-cycle state does not produce false-positive missing-findings blocks.
- Resource: test step execution path. Interaction: a524-fded migrates test execution to a background primitive. Gate: the wrapper for the test step captures full output regardless of whether the underlying test command runs synchronously or backgrounded.
- Resource: skipped-step structural records. Interaction: a154-98de PRECONDITIONS degradation channel introduces structural attestation for graceful-degradation paths. Gate: SC5 skipped:<reason> markers conform to the same schema as PRECONDITIONS attestation records, or the schemas are explicitly aligned in a follow-up.
- Resource: silent-skip detection psychology. Interaction: e884-d0ad PostToolUse forced next-step reminder targets the same root-cause failure mode at a different point in the loop. Gate: pre-commit verifier and PostToolUse reminder do not double-fire on the same skip event; one is authoritative for any given skip class.
- Resource: commit message construction order. Interaction: 170b-2ac9 commit-level source attribution via git-native trailers. Gate: artifact verification runs before trailer injection; ordering documented in COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md.
- Resource: breadcrumb log format. Interaction: 5df7-63ac integrated observability. Gate: breadcrumb log entries written by wrappers include observability-compatible fields (timestamp, step name, agent context, optional cost hooks) so 5df7-63ac can consume the same log without duplicating infrastructure.
- Resource: wrapper-written artifact metadata. Interaction: e407-d35c source attribution. Gate: wrapper artifacts include attribution metadata fields (skill name, agent ID, sub-agent context) that e407-d35c can read without separate metadata files.
- Resource: classifier / reviewer dispatch interface. Interaction: f9f8-a15c-79e0-4dc3 add Gemini provider to CI LLM review provider abstraction. Gate: wrapper output capture for classifier and reviewer dispatch is provider-agnostic; the artifact contract does not depend on a specific provider.
- Resource: hook installation pipeline. Interaction: 87e9-0bc8 polyglot test gate modifies reinstall-hooks.sh. Gate: the new pre-commit verifier registers via the same install path; hook execution order documented so polyglot test-gate and verifier compose deterministically.
- Resource: pre-commit gate execution order. Interaction: 88d2-6756 / jira-dig-1671 required CodeQL + code-quality scanning gates. Gate: artifact verification, CodeQL scanning, and other pre-commit gates each run as discrete steps that compose; no implicit dependence on each other's output beyond pass/fail signaling.
- Resource: reviewer override semantics. Interaction: jira-dig-1673 reviewer override discipline. Gate: dso commit-override composes with — does not bypass — reviewer override discipline; user-invoked override does not silently dismiss reviewer findings; produces an audit record both gates can consume.
- Resource: REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md overlay-dispatch verified-artifact set. Interaction: cbea-3722 ACCESSIBILITY_REVIEWER agent integration. Gate: when accessibility reviewer is dispatched as part of REVIEW Step 4b, its findings file is part of the verified-artifact set; missing accessibility-findings.json (when accessibility was flagged) triggers the same block as missing security-redteam-findings.json.

## Scenario Analysis

11 surviving failure scenarios from red/blue team filter (16 raised; 5 filtered as speculative or already-handled).

Critical:
- CWD mismatch fast-fail triggers inside legitimate sub-agent worktrees during harvest — wrapper's CWD check must compare resolved target artifacts dir's worktree root, not process CWD, or every harvest invocation rejects.
- New pre-commit hook not executable after fresh clone or plugin sync overwrites it — git silently skips non-executable hooks; entire load-bearing gate is bypassed without error.

High:
- Artifact write and pre-commit hook read race under parallel sub-agent harvest; spurious gate failures during in-flight harvests.
- Wrapper artifact write swallowed when underlying command times out (~73s ceiling); missing artifact with no diagnostic trail.
- a524-fded background test primitive output not captured when test runs detached; empty/stub artifact misinterpreted as test failure.
- ARTIFACTS_DIR undefined in CI environment causes hook to crash or resolve to wrong path.
- Hook added after existing pre-commit hook causes silent override of prior hook chain in host projects.
- First-run artifact directory missing causes hook to block all commits before any wrapper has run.
- commands.test_changed unset causes wrapper to emit no artifact and hook to block instead of skip.
- review.max_resolution_attempts exhaustion + verifier block produces deadlock — agent has no automated path to unblock.
- Breadcrumb log path diverges between wrapper write and hook read when worktree uses non-default branch name with special characters.

### Planning Intelligence Log

- **Web research (Step 2.6)**: not triggered
  - Bright-line conditions that fired: none (no third-party API, no new dependency, no auth/credentials, no migration; wrapper pattern is established internally via existing test-gate / review-gate)
- **Scenario analysis (Step 2.75)**: triggered
  - Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 11 (of 16 red team findings)
- **Practitioner-requested additional cycles**: cross-epic scan re-triggered via gate (manual triage initially; full classifier dispatch on practitioner authorization, surfacing 1 additional ambiguity (f61f-7e0a-36d3-4e7d) and 8 additional considerations injected as Cross-Epic Interactions ACs)
- **Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0)**: triggered — depth: 0 (forbidden-action HARD-GATE follow-on stub created as af26-dd5a-df6d-4f81; scrutiny intentionally skipped at practitioner's direction)
- **Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5)**: not triggered
- **LLM-instruction signal (Step 5)**: triggered — keyword: hook behavioral logic (bot-psychologist Probe B during pre-Phase 1 covered the orchestrator behavioral surface; concrete prompt edits will go through plan-review during /dso:preplanning)
- **Scale context (Step 0)**: not applicable (developer-tooling feature; per-invocation overhead matters but no record/traffic axis)
data.title: Make HARD-GATE per-step workflow compliance load-bearing via wrapper-driven artifact verification
